title: pastebox: let pastes expire
intent: pastebox keeps every paste until someone deletes it, and the issue reports a disk 90% full. This guided plan lets the writer pick when a paste expires, deletes expired pastes in a cleanup job, and keeps never as the default.

ISSUE.label: The issue: pastes never go away
quote: pastes are kept until someone deletes them, and almost nobody does

PLAN-FORM.label: The plan: the new choice on the form
PLAN-FORM.quote: The new paste form gets an "Expires after" choice: 1 hour, 1 day, 1 week, or never. Never is selected first.

PLAN-COLUMN.label: The plan: the new column
quote: It stays empty for a paste that never expires, and for every paste saved before this change.

PLAN-410.label: The plan: what an expired paste answers

PLAN-JOB.label: The plan: the cleanup job
quote: A cleanup job runs every 10 minutes and deletes the pastes whose `expires_at` has passed.
After that, the link answers 404, like any missing paste.

PLAN-KEPT.label: The plan: what does not change
quote: Deleting a paste by hand works as before.

PLAN-OPEN.label: The plan: the open question
quote: an expired paste answers 410 until the cleanup job runs, then 404
Should it answer 404 from the start, so the answer never changes?
The maintainers decide before the release.

README.label: pastebox's README
README.quote: Pastes are kept until someone deletes them.

overview.text: A paste can expire after 1 hour, 1 day or 1 week. Never stays the default.
The new paste form gets an Expires after choice.
The table gets an `expires_at` column, and an expired paste answers 410.
A cleanup job deletes expired pastes every 10 minutes.
Pastes saved before the change never expire, and deleting by hand works as before.
Should an expired paste answer 404 from the start?

sections.heading: Every paste, kept forever
sections.lead: pastebox keeps a paste until someone deletes it, and almost nobody does. The issue reports a disk 90% full and asks for pastes that expire.

cards.title: Where pastes are kept
body: Every paste is one row in the `pastes` table: an id, the text, and when it was saved. Nothing records how long to keep it.

cards.title: What the issue asks
body: A choice on the form, with never as the default, so nothing changes for anyone who does not pick.

sections.title: The server and the table
sections.heading: Expired pastes answer 410
sections.lead: The `pastes` table gets an `expires_at` column. Reading a paste whose time has passed answers 410 Gone, and a cleanup job runs every 10 minutes to delete it.

figure.title: Every route, today and after
figure.caption: Only the reads answer differently. Deleting by hand works as before.

cards.title: The check on every read
body: Today a read answers 404 when the row is missing. The expiry check goes right beside it. The raw route calls the same function, so it gets the check too.

figure.title: Reading a paste in src/store.js
text: const row = db.get("SELECT body FROM pastes WHERE id = ?", id);
figure.caption: The expiry check goes beside the missing check, and the raw route inherits it.

cards.title: A paste's life
body: Once its time passes, a paste answers 410. The cleanup job then deletes the row, and the same link answers 404.

figure.caption: The answer changes from 410 to 404 when the job runs. The last section asks about that.

sections.question: Should an expired paste answer 404 from the start?
sections.lead: As written, an expired paste answers 410 until the cleanup job runs, then 404. Answering 404 from the start means the answer never changes. The maintainers decide before the release.
